images.title: The centre of 2, 6, 10 and 12 is 7.5
images.purpose: Shows that the mean balances the distances even when it falls between the dots.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One wide number line across the middle of the frame with four dots above it and a small balance triangle under the mean; four short distance arrows into the mean.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 0 to 14 with 15 evenly spaced short tick marks, one at each whole number; no numbers under the ticks except the four listed. Four equal teal (#0072B2) dots sit just above the line, one each at 2, 6, 10 and 12, with the numbers 2, 6, 10 and 12 printed under their ticks. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) solid triangle sits under the line with its tip touching the line at 7.5, exactly halfway between the ticks for 7 and 8, with the label mean 7.5 under it. Four thin unlabelled amber (#E69F00) arrows run just above the line, one from each dot to the point 7.5: from 2 and from 6 on the left, from 10 and from 12 on the right. Above the left pair of arrows, centred, the label 5.5 + 1.5 = 7; above the right pair, centred, the label 2.5 + 4.5 = 7. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The mean 7.5 sits between the dots, and the distances on each side both add to 7.
images.description: Shows that the mean balances the distances even when it falls between the dots.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to add the distances on each side before reading the two sums.

image_decisions.why: A dot plot with the balance point between two dots shows at once that the mean need not be one of the values.
